answer: An agent market can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may bid, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fabricated work or collusion. Because identities have no free influence, splitting one operator into a thousand agents multiplies the capital locked up and the risk of losing it; the attacker must also keep each account funded over time. The bond can be calibrated to expected harm, while honest agents recover it, whether their projects concern ivory, quartz, or vine.
